PROPERTY TRANSFER FEE
The Dubai Land Department charges a transfer fee of 4% of the property purchase price.
This fee is typically split equally between buyer (2%) and seller (2%) by mutual agreement,
though the full 4% may be borne by one party based on contract terms.

Additional administrative fees apply:
- Properties valued up to AED 500,000: AED 4,000 admin fee
- Properties valued above AED 500,000: AED 580 admin fee (knowledge fee) + AED 4,000 registration

MORTGAGE REGISTRATION FEE
If the property is purchased with mortgage financing:
- 0.25% of the total loan amount
- Minimum fee: AED 1,000
- Maximum fee: No cap
Example: AED 1,500,000 mortgage = AED 3,750 mortgage registration fee

TITLE DEED ISSUANCE
- Title deed fee: AED 250
- Map issuance: AED 250 (for land) or AED 100 (for unit)
- Typing fee: AED 4,000 for non-off-plan properties

OFF-PLAN REGISTRATION (OQOOD)
For properties purchased directly from developers:
- Registration fee: 4% of sale price
- Oqood registration: AED 3,010 (villas/townhouses) or AED 1,020 (apartments)
- This registers the Sales and Purchase Agreement (SPA) on the DLD system

NOC (NO OBJECTION CERTIFICATE) FROM DEVELOPER
Required before title deed transfer in managed communities:
- Fee range: AED 500 to AED 5,000 (developer-dependent)
- Processing time: 5 to 15 working days
- Outstanding service charges must be cleared before NOC is issued
- Without NOC, DLD will not process the transfer

VALUATION FEE
For mortgage properties, a DLD-approved valuation is required:
- Independent valuation cost: AED 2,500 to AED 3,500
- Bank-arranged valuation may be included in mortgage processing fee

IMPORTANT TIMELINES
- Title deed registration must be completed within 30 days of signing the MOU
- Off-plan SPA must be registered within 30 days of signing
- Mortgage must be registered within 30 days of title deed transfer

The UAE Central Bank regulates all mortgage lending through Circular 28/2013.

- First property up to AED 5M: maximum 80% LTV (20% down payment)

INDIVIDUAL OWNERSHIP

RERA — REAL ESTATE REGULATORY AGENCY COMPLETE GUIDE

WHAT IS RERA?
RERA (Real Estate Regulatory Agency) is the regulatory arm of the Dubai Land Department (DLD).
Established in 2007, RERA governs all real estate activity in Dubai including:
- Developer registration and project approvals
- Broker and agent licensing
- Rental regulations (RERA rental index)
- Dispute resolution
- Off-plan escrow management

DEVELOPER REQUIREMENTS
Before selling any off-plan property, developers must:
1. Register the project with RERA (get RERA project number)
2. Obtain all construction permits from relevant authorities
3. Open a RERA-approved escrow account (funds held separately)
4. Show proof of land ownership or long-term lease
5. Obtain DLD approval for sales launch
6. Register all sales staff as licensed real estate brokers

ESCROW ACCOUNT REQUIREMENTS
- Developer cannot access escrow funds until construction milestones are reached
- DLD appoints independent escrow auditors
- Buyer funds are protected if developer defaults
- Escrow releases: 20% on foundation, 30% on structure, 30% on completion, 20% on handover

BROKER AND AGENT LICENSING
All real estate brokers in Dubai must:
- Pass the RERA exam (Certified Real Estate Broker)
- Register with Dubai Land Department
- Obtain a RERA broker card (renewed annually)
- Work under a licensed real estate company (brokerage)
- Display RERA card number on all marketing materials

HOW TO VERIFY BROKER CREDENTIALS
- Dubai REST app: Search broker by name or RERA number
- DLD website: Broker verification portal
- Report unlicensed brokers: 800-DLD (800-353)

RENTAL REGULATIONS
Rental Increase Calculator: RERA provides an official rental index
- If current rent is within 10% of RERA index: 0% increase allowed
- If rent is 11-20% below index: Maximum 5% increase
- If rent is 21-30% below index: Maximum 10% increase

STRATA LAW AND OWNERS ASSOCIATIONS — DUBAI
===========================================

JOINTLY OWNED PROPERTY LAW
Dubai Law No. 27 of 2007 governs all jointly owned properties.
Jointly owned = any development with shared common areas (apartments, gated communities).

OWNERS ASSOCIATION (OA) — WHAT IS IT?
Every jointly owned development MUST have a registered Owners Association.
OA is a legal entity representing all property owners in that development.
Registered with and supervised by RERA.

OA STRUCTURE
Developer phase (before 75% units sold):
- Developer acts as interim OA manager
- Must register with RERA within 60 days of first sale

After 75% sold:
- Elections held — owners vote for OA board
- Minimum 3, maximum 7 board members
- Board members must be owners in the development
- Board elects: Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Secretary, Treasurer

Annual General Meeting (AGM):
- Required by law every year
- 30 days written notice to all owners
- Agenda: Budget approval, board elections, major decisions
- Quorum: 25% of owners (or 10% for second notice if first meeting fails)

OA MANAGEMENT COMPANY
OA hires a licensed management company (not the same as developer):
- Licensed by RERA
- Manages day-to-day operations
- Prepares annual budget
- Collects service charges
- Coordinates maintenance contractors

BUDGET AND SERVICE CHARGES
Management company prepares annual budget:
- General Fund: Day-to-day expenses (cleaning, security, landscaping, utilities)
- Reserve Fund: Future major repairs (10-15% of total budget minimum)
- Budget must be approved at AGM
- Service charges calculated per sqft based on approved budget

RERA DISPUTE RESOLUTION FOR SERVICE CHARGES
If you disagree with service charge amount:
1. Write to OA/management company first
2. If unresolved: File complaint with RERA (RDC — Registration and Dispute Centre)
3. RERA can review and adjust if charges are unreasonable
4. Maximum charges are guided by RERA published rates

- No pets (unless building is pet-friendly)
- No commercial activities from residential units

- Typically charged per square foot of the property

- Divided into: General fund (routine maintenance) + Reserve fund (major replacements)
